plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 20 = $13.33. To maximize profit, I should bid just above this, but capping it to my value. Therefore, I will bid $13.40.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and the payment rule (paying the second-highest bid), the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, and with three bidders, a conservative estimate of the second highest bid is around $6.7. However, my value is $35, so I can afford to bid higher. I will bid a value close to my private value, but not exceeding it, to maximize profit.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly lower bid, while bidding above your value risks overpaying. Since this is the only round, there's no opportunity to learn and adjust. My value is $37, so I bid $37.
